action.check.value: Choose the answer supported by the example.

action.execute.value: Run it in your tool and record observed behavior, expected behavior and the repeat check. Say if you have not run it.

action.learn.value: Read the example and identify the expected result.

action.prepare.value: Adapt the request using fictional data and record your response.

app.deliver.value: Deliver the folder and instructions for opening, testing and stopping the server, with passes/failures. To share a static app, use the site lesson's Netlify flow without repeating that lesson: upload the folder with index.html, check visibility and test the URL as a visitor. Each browser has its own data; local-address data does not automatically migrate to the published URL. Test reload at the final origin. Login and sync would require another project.

app.execute.value: To serve the app, first ask the AI to check Python 3; when available, run `python3 -m http.server 8000` in tarefas-app (Windows: `py -3 -m http.server 8000`) and open `http://localhost:8000`. Stop with Ctrl+C in the terminal running the server. If Python is missing, request an available local preview or an explained alternative before installing anything. Review the plan and allow building in the folder. Ask the AI to start a local server, provide its address and explain how to stop it and any required dependencies. Open that address. Test empty input and spaces: no task should be created. Add two tasks, complete one, reload and check both plus completion. Remove one and reload. Example failure: completion disappears. Correction: ‘After completing and reloading, the task becomes pending. Preserve add/remove; save and restore completion too.’ Repeat the whole sequence. Use the same origin/address when comparing persistence.

app.learn.value: An app changes state when someone acts. Here, state means the task list and completed tasks. Persistence keeps data after reload. Create tarefas-app. Use fictional data. localStorage stores data in this browser and origin; it does not sync accounts/devices and can be cleared. Do not use this prototype for important information.

app.objective.value: Create interaction, validate input and check local persistence.

app.prepare.value: Request: ‘Create a dependency-free task app in index.html: labeled input, Add button, list, complete/uncomplete and remove. Reject empty or whitespace-only input with a clear message. Save tasks and completion in localStorage; restore on opening. If stored data is invalid or saving fails, notify without crashing. No login or server. Explain running at a stable local address and testing.’ Simulated example: adding ‘Study’ shows one row; completing marks it; reload keeps the completed row; remove and reload leaves an empty list. These are expected results, not recorded execution.

app.q1.value: What should submitting only spaces do?

app.q1.b.value: Show guidance and leave the list without a new task.

app.q1.feedback.value: The second answer validates input without destroying valid state. Creating an empty item or clearing the list misses the goal.

app.q2.value: A task appears before reload and disappears afterward. What is the correct conclusion?

app.q2.c.value: Adding worked in that session; saving/restoring still needs fixing and retesting.

app.q2.feedback.value: The third answer identifies the evidence limit. Seeing an item once does not prove persistence; compare the same origin before and after reload.

automation.deliver.value: Deliver the fictional CSV, script, report.md and exact run instructions, with normal/repeat/error test results. Someone should be able to repeat using the folder. Do not claim scheduling because a script ran once. If scheduling later, define time/time zone, folder, computer availability, where to inspect results/errors and how to pause; observe one triggered run before relying on it. This beta teaches verifiable manual delivery; it does not run schedules or send reports for you.

automation.execute.value: Ask the AI to check `python3 --version` (Windows: `py -3 --version`). With Python 3 available, request `python3 report.py vendas.csv report.md` in relatorio (Windows: `py -3 report.py vendas.csv report.md`). A terminal is the command area; the tool can run commands for you and show output. If Python is missing, request an alternative: local HTML that accepts the same CSV in a browser, applies the same rules and offers report.md for download without installing packages. Open the HTML, select the CSV and save the result; on error, do not download a replacement. Review and run the provided command in the selected folder through the tool. If the environment is missing, request instructions for your system; record the error instead of claiming execution. Open report.md and compare count/total with the calculation. Run again: still 2 and 30.50. Copy the CSV, remove amount and run: it should report an error and preserve the previous report. Restore the copy and repeat. If it duplicates or overwrites on error, provide input, actual result and expected rule; request correction and repeat all three tests.

automation.learn.value: Automation is a repeatable procedure: input, transformation and output. Start by running manually; scheduling only repeats an already-correct process. Create relatorio. CSV is a text table: the first row names columns, later rows hold records. Use the example below, decimal points and fictional data. Expected result: two valid records, total 30.50; no message sent.

automation.objective.value: Turn a CSV into a verifiable report and repeat without duplication.

automation.prepare.value: Request: ‘Create vendas.csv with id,item,amount and rows 1,Caderno,10.50 and 2,Curso,20.00. Create report.py in Python 3 without external packages, accepting input and output arguments, to read this CSV, validate columns/values, count records and sum amount using decimal precision. Generate report.md with count 2 and total 30.50. Rerunning must replace the report without duplication. If a column is missing or a value invalid, show an error and preserve the last valid report. Explain dependencies, command and working folder; do not send data or schedule.’ Simulated output: Records: 2; Total: 30.50. Reference calculation: 10.50 + 20.00 = 30.50.

automation.q1.value: What is correct on the second run of the same CSV?

automation.q1.b.value: 2 records and total 30.50, replacing the report.

automation.q1.c.value: No file, because it already ran once.

automation.q1.feedback.value: The second answer repeats without duplication. Adding to the old report duplicates data; producing no output does not ensure an updated deliverable.

automation.q2.value: The amount column was removed. Which behavior meets the rule?

automation.q2.a.value: Generate zero and replace the valid report.

automation.q2.c.value: Report the error, preserve the valid report and allow the input to be corrected.

automation.q2.feedback.value: The third answer makes failure visible without destroying the last valid output. Silent zeros and invented values hide the error.

course.summary.value: Hackathon beta: four practical lessons. Original simulated examples; external execution is self-reported. AI translation, human review pending.

course.title.value: Sites, apps and automations with AI

criterion.record.value: A record of what you actually ran

foundations.deliver.value: Deliver the request, received plan and comparison. Separate what you checked in the text from what a page still needs to demonstrate. To switch tools, keep the request and criteria but check the context again. Continue with the site, app or automation route; none requires completing the others.

foundations.execute.value: Send the request in the chosen folder. Read the response: title? three services? contact without sending? Answer relevant questions with fictional data. Compare and request a specific correction. Read the new list. If editing is proposed, return to planning. Record a before/after excerpt; if all criteria already pass, explain why. Do not invent a failure just to complete the record.

foundations.learn.value: You need a computer, browser and installed Claude Desktop or Codex Desktop, signed in with access to development features. Check access conditions and costs first; this lesson does not promise free use. A folder holds project files; context is the location and information the AI works with. Create a ganesha-pratica folder in your file manager and select it in the tool. Use an account with access. If login or a plan restriction appears, resolve access or use the simulation; do not count that as execution. A plan describes intended work. A working page requires files and testing.

foundations.objective.value: Set context, request a plan and correct a response.

foundations.prepare.value: Request: ‘Plan a Ponte Musical page for beginners: title, guitar, piano and singing; contact reveals aulas@example.com without sending a message. Return a list and future tests. Do not edit files or publish.’ Simulated response: correct title, guitar and piano, a form that sends a message. Comparison: singing is missing and the form exceeds scope. Correction: ‘Keep the title, add singing and replace the form with the displayed address; update the tests.’ Simulated revised plan: title, three services, contact reveals the address, future click test.

foundations.q1.value: The plan omits singing and collects a phone number. Which correction meets the request?

foundations.q1.a.value: Remove the phone field and keep only two services.

foundations.q1.b.value: Keep the title, add singing and show the address without collection or sending.

foundations.q1.c.value: Add singing and test sending the phone number.

foundations.q1.feedback.value: The second answer fixes both deviations. The first still omits singing; the third retains an unrequested action.

foundations.q2.value: The revised plan lists every item. What does that establish?

foundations.q2.a.value: Contact already works in the browser.

foundations.q2.c.value: The text meets the compared criteria; behavior still needs execution.

foundations.q2.feedback.value: The third answer separates planning from functioning. Text and a proposed test do not prove a click or publication.

hint.compare.value: Compare the result with the criteria, not just the AI message.

hint.repair.value: For errors, describe reproduction steps, actual and expected behavior; request a specific change and repeat the test.

notice.simulated.value: Original exercise. Described results are simulated examples, not execution records. Ganesha neither operates your tool nor automatically verifies your work.

site.deliver.value: After local testing, sign in to Netlify and open https://app.netlify.com/drop. Upload the folder containing index.html directly. Wait for the URL. Check project visibility; if public access is intended and permitted, use Make public. Open the URL without the owner's session and test contact. A URL alone does not prove public access. To update, test locally then upload the folder under Production deploys in the same project: this changes production. Check the new version at the URL. For missing files or blank pages, check the uploaded folder. Deliver the URL and test results, or the tested folder and the recorded publishing obstacle.

site.execute.value: Review the plan, request creation and inspect changed files. Open index.html from your file manager in a browser. Count the three services; click Contact; reload and use Tab to reach the button, then Enter. Narrow the window: are text and button usable? For failure, send steps, actual and expected behavior to the AI; reopen the correct file and repeat the same tests. ‘Fixed’ from the AI does not replace observation.

site.learn.value: A static site can use one index.html: structure, appearance and a browser interaction. This exercise needs no visitor account or data server. Create ponte-site. Result: Ponte Musical title, three services and a button revealing the fictional address. Include no forms, sending or credentials. Keep a copy before changes.

site.objective.value: Build, test, fix and publish a static page.

site.prepare.value: Complete request: ‘In ponte-site, create a self-contained index.html with title Ponte Musical, guitar/piano/singing services and a Contact button revealing aulas@example.com. No external libraries, data collection or sending. Use a keyboard-accessible button and a layout fitting narrow screens. Explain opening and testing. Describe the plan first.’ Simulated example: file created, three cards and a button. Simulated failure: clicking does not reveal the address. Correction: ‘Opening index.html and clicking Contact shows nothing; I expect the address. Fix only that, preserve the services and repeat the test.’ Expected corrected result: visible address.

site.q1.value: Which test checks the main action?

site.q1.b.value: Click and observe the address; repeat using the keyboard.

site.q1.feedback.value: The second answer checks behavior. A visible button or AI assertion does not demonstrate the action.

site.q2.value: The URL opens for the owner but asks another visitor to log in. What next?

site.q2.a.value: Check visibility/permissions and retry without the owner's session.

site.q2.c.value: Upload the same files again without checking access.

site.q2.feedback.value: The first answer investigates the actual obstacle. Authenticated access does not prove public availability; another upload may not fix visibility.

tool.claude.value: Claude Desktop: open Code, choose Local and the exercise folder. For planning only, choose Plan; for building, review the plan and permissions before allowing changes. Access depends on your account.

tool.codex.value: Codex Desktop: select Codex and open the exercise folder/project. Check the context before sending. Request planning only when appropriate; do not assume its controls match Claude's.
